items.description: EL2 hypervisor and toolchain that boots macOS on the ASUS A16 (Snapdragon X2 Elite), with an Adreno Metal/IOGPU stack
items.readme:
# Snapintosh ![Snapintosh — macOS on Snapdragon; ASCII hands reaching toward a red chip](docs/assets/snapintosh-ascii-chip-red.png) Snapintosh boots Apple's macOS 27 (build 26A428) on an ASUS Zenbook A16 laptop with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite (X2E-96-100). It is an EL2 monitor (hypervisor) and the toolchain around it. The monitor runs Apple's stock kernelcache (the J700/T8140 kernel) unmodified by default. It supplies the platform contracts that the kernel expects from Apple silicon: the SPTM and TXM monitor calls, translation of the kernel's 16 KiB page tables, and the Apple devices the kernel looks for. Graphics run on the laptop's own Adreno X2-90 GPU through a driver stack written for this project: - **AdrenoMetal.bundle**: a Metal driver plug-in. - **AdrenoX2**: an IOGPU kernel extension, with **AdrenoDisplay** driving the internal panel. - **air2ir3**: a shader compiler that translates Apple's AIR (Metal's IR) into Mesa's ir3 for the Adreno. There is no software, CPU or paravirtual rendering path. The project also includes an I2C-HID keyboard and touchpad driver (SnapI2CHID), native QCC2072 Wi-Fi work, and NVMe storage through an emulated Apple storage controller. Snapintosh is used together with [q1n1](https://github.com/Acelogic/q1n1), a UEFI EL2 proxy forked from Asahi Linux's m1n1. q1n1 takes the machine at EL2 after UEFI and serves m1n1's proxy protocol over USB-C to a Mac host, which drives Snapintosh from there. ## Status This is experimental software, written for one laptop model. | Area | State | | --- | --- | | macOS desktop on the A16 | Boots to the desktop with GPU acceleration. Rendering is correct: the pixel checks across the desktop test scenes pass. | | Smoothness | In progress. Interaction is usable but not yet smooth. The target is a steady ~60 Hz first and the panel's 120 Hz later. | | Input | The built-in keyboard and touchpad work, including trackpad gestures, Mission Control and app switching. | | Wi-Fi (QCC2072) | Scanning, a WPA2 connection, DHCP and ping work through a host-proxy harness driven from the Mac. Joining from the macOS Wi-Fi menu does not work yet. | | Storage | macOS is installed on, and boots from, the internal NVMe. | | Other hardware | Audio, cameras, Bluetooth, sleep and external displays are not supported. | [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the details, the known issues and the roadmap. ## Required hardware - An **ASUS Zenbook A16 with the Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E-96-100** (UX3607OA). Nothing else is supported. The monitor, device tables, clocks and register addresses are specific to this machine. - A **Mac host** running macOS 27, connected to the A16 over USB-C. q1n1 brings up a USB NCM network link on that cable, and every boot, upload and log capture goes over it. - AC power is strongly recommended. The tools refuse to boot or write the SSD below a battery threshold. ## Architecture in brief ```mermaid flowchart TD UEFI["A16 UEFI firmware"] --> Q1N1 Q1N1["q1n1: UEFI EL2 proxy
(USB-C NCM link to the Mac host)"] --> MON MON["Snapintosh EL2 monitor
SPTM/TXM call emulation, 16K-to-4K shadow page tables,
Apple device models (AIC, ANS2 NVMe, DART, ...), GPU ring and SMMU mediation"] --> XNU XNU["Stock macOS kernel at EL1 + AuxKC
(AdrenoX2 + AdrenoDisplay, SnapI2CHID, ...)"] --> USER USER["macOS userspace
WindowServer, Core Animation, apps
AdrenoMetal.bundle + air2ir3 compiler runtime"] HOST["Mac host: tools/cycle.py, q1n1 proxy client"] -. USB-C NCM .-> Q1N1 ``` ``` A16 UEFI -> q1n1 (EL2 proxy) -> Snapintosh monitor (EL2) -> XNU + AuxKC (EL1) -> userspace + Metal plug-in (EL0) ``` [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains each layer. ## Repository layout | Path | Contents | | --- | --- | | `compat/` | the EL2 monitor: SPTM/TXM contracts, CPU, interrupt, timer and device emulation, the GPU ring and SMMU mediation, the NVMe backend | | `shadow/` | the page-table walker and the 16 KiB guest to 4 KiB hardware shadow tables | | `probes/` | the code that runs on the target (loader, monitor entry) and the host-side image builder and runner | | `tools/` | firmware acquisition, kernelcache analysis, the boot-cycle tool (`cycle.py`), build helpers and the native test suites | | `gpu/adreno-kext/` | the AdrenoX2 kext (`kext/`), the AdrenoMetal plug-in (`plugin/`) and the shared register and contract headers | | `gpu/air2ir3/` | the AIR to ir3 shader compiler ([README](gpu/air2ir3/README.md)) | | `gpu/agx*` | an earlier virtual-AGX model, kept for reference | | `drivers/` | smaller kexts: SnapI2CHID (`snap-i2c-hid/`), the QCC2072 Wi-Fi controller (`snap-qcc2072/`), the boot framebuffer, a loader test | | `config/` | monitor feature flags and guest launchd jobs | | `build/` | generated output (gitignored, apart from the AuxKC link helpers) | | `docs/` | design and reference documentation | ## Building You need: - a Mac with Xcode (macOS 27 SDK); - the Kernel Debug Kit for build 26A428, installed at `/Library/Developer/KDKs/KDK_27.0_26A428.kdk`; - Python 3; - Homebrew LLVM, Meson and Ninja for the shader compiler. Its Mesa checkout is fetched and patched by `gpu/air2ir3/tools/mesa-setup.sh`; - a q1n1 checkout next to this one (`../q1n1`). [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) has the steps. ## Bring your own Apple software This repository ships **no Apple, Qualcomm or ASUS binaries or firmware**. You supply them yourself: - **The macOS 27 restore image (IPSW).** Download it from Apple with `python3 tools/fetch-ipsw.py [destination]`. Then extract the J700 boot set (kernelcache, device tree, SPTM, TXM and others) with `python3 tools/extract-firmware.py j700ap`. Nothing runs without it. - **The Kernel Debug Kit** for 26A428, from Apple's developer downloads. - **Device firmware.** The Adreno GPU's GMU and SQE microcode (`gen80100_gmu.bin`, `gen80100_sqe.fw`) and the QCC2072 Wi-Fi firmware come from the linux-firmware project. The Wi-Fi board file (`bdwlan_qcc2072_1p0_ncm820A.elf`) comes from ASUS's Windows WLAN driver package for this model. The tools check each file against a pinned SHA-256. The project depends on Apple software that each user must obtain and use under Apple's terms. ## Warning Snapintosh is an experimental hypervisor that runs with full control of the machine. - **It writes the internal NVMe SSD.** Installing macOS changes the partition table, and the guest writes its own volumes. A bug can corrupt or destroy data on the SSD, including the Windows installation. Back up everything before you start, and keep a way to restore Windows. - It programs clocks, voltages, the GPU and memory-bandwidth votes directly. The tools refuse to run on low battery and stop the run when the SoC gets too hot (`--thermal-guard`), but those guards are not a guarantee. - It is not a supported or stable way to run macOS. Expect panics, hangs and cold reboots. Use it at your own risk. ## Legal Snapintosh is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Apple, Qualcomm, ASUS or Asahi Linux. macOS, Metal and Apple are trademarks of Apple Inc. Snapdragon and Adreno are trademarks of Qualcomm Incorporated. Zenbook is a trademark of ASUSTeK Computer Inc. All other trademarks belong to their owners. Running macOS on non-Apple hardware may conflict with Apple's macOS software licence agreement. You are responsible for making sure that your use complies with the licences that apply to you. ## License The project's own code is MIT licensed; see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Some components carry other licences. Generated Mesa register tables keep Mesa's MIT notice, and the QEMU tracer patch in `tools/qemu-sptm-oracle/` is GPL-2.0-or-later. [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [LICENSES/](LICENSES/) list every third-party component and its licence text. ## Credits Snapintosh builds on the published work of others: - **Asahi Linux and m1n1.** q1n1 is a fork of m1n1, and Snapintosh uses m1n1's proxy protocol, its Apple-silicon constants and its RTKit/mailbox knowledge. - **Mesa and freedreno**, for the ir3 compiler that air2ir3 builds on, the Adreno register database and the a6xx/a8xx driver code used as reference. - **The Linux msm/drm, clk/qcom, ath12k, i2c-hid and GENI driver authors.** Their drivers were read as hardware references. Snapintosh's drivers are written from the interface facts, and one generated table is derived from Linux's Adreno catalogue (see the notices). - **jprx**, for [qemu-sptm](https://github.com/jprx/qemu-sptm) and [darwin-vm](https://github.com/jprx/darwin-vm), used to observe Apple's real SPTM/TXM as ground truth. - **XNU** sources from Apple Open Source, for reading the kernel's side of each contract. [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) has the complete list. ## Documentation | Read | For | | --- | --- | | [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) | what works, known issues, roadmap | | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | how the layers fit together, including the GPU stack and Wi-Fi | | [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md) | building the monitor, kexts, plug-in and compiler | | [docs/RUNNING.md](docs/RUNNING.md) | a boot cycle with `tools/cycle.py` | | [docs/KERNEL-PATCHES.md](docs/KERNEL-PATCHES.md) | the opt-in kernel patches and why each exists | | [docs/BOOT-CHAIN.md](docs/BOOT-CHAIN.md) | how a stock macOS kernel boots on this SoC | | [docs/FULL-INSTALL.md](docs/FULL-INSTALL.md) | installing to and booting from the internal NVMe | | [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) | guest/host boundaries and pinned profiles | | [gpu/air2ir3/README.md](gpu/air2ir3/README.md) | the shader compiler | | [docs/WORKSPACE-LAYOUT.md](docs/WORKSPACE-LAYOUT.md) | local inputs, generated output and what is never committed | | [docs/GUI-BOOT-ROADMAP.md](docs/GUI-BOOT-ROADMAP.md) | the path from the first kernel instruction to the desktop |

items.name: hackios-xnu-kernel
items.readme:
# HackiOS — XNU kernel **HackiOS** boots Apple's open-source **XNU kernel** (`xnu-8796.121.2`, the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone hardware and runs the **unmodified iOS 16.5 user space** on top of it: launchd → backboardd → SpringBoard → apps. Our own EFI loader, our own replacements for Apple's closed drivers, a UEFI port, and a Linux Wi-Fi driver on a compatibility layer make that possible. It runs in two places: - **POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood, Snapdragon 778G)** — nothing is flashed: the UEFI is started with `fastboot boot`, the whole system lives in RAM, and after a reboot the phone is back in Android; - **QEMU** (`virt`, aarch64) — the same thing on any Linux computer, no phone needed. This repository is half of the project: | Repository | What | |---|---| | **hackios-xnu-kernel** (this one) | XNU patches, the EFI loader, the UEFI port, Wi-Fi, QEMU scripts, `xl`, prebuilt kernel/loader/UEFI, `common/` scripts | | [hackios-xnu-userland](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-userland) | our init, injected libraries, launchd jobs, the APFS image builder, the scripts that take iOS out of Apple's IPSW, Metal/Mesa work | > **No Apple files are in either repository.** `ios165/fetch.sh` downloads the iOS 16.5 IPSW from Apple's own CDN > to *your* machine and extracts what is needed there. HackiOS is an independent research project by OOSEX GANG and > is not affiliated with, authorised or endorsed by Apple Inc. iOS, iPhone and Apple are trademarks of Apple Inc.

Photographed on the phone, the Adreno GPU drawing (`gpu=1`). More in [Screenshots](#screenshots). ## What works | Works | Does not work (yet) | |---|---| | Lock screen, swipe to unlock, home screen with all icons (two pages), stock iOS 16 wallpapers | Cellular, Bluetooth | | System gestures: swipe up (home, app switcher), edge swipe (back), Control Center | Charging under our kernel (the phone only discharges) | | Apps: Settings, Clock, Calendar, Photos, Notes, Safari and more; widgets (Weather, Calendar) on the phone | Metal for apps (in progress: 293 of 456 system shaders already run on the Adreno, see `docs/air.md` in hackios-xnu-userland) | | Phone touchscreen (Goodix GT9916), multitouch, wake on touch; real power and volume keys | App Store content and Apple ID sign-in (no Secure Enclave; FairPlay daemon exits) | | Up to 8 CPU cores (`cpus=8`), big core at 2.4 GHz, ~20 s to the lock screen | Video and Live Photo recording | | Adreno 642L GPU through Mesa/freedreno (`gpu=1`, OpenGL ES for CoreAnimation) | | | Wi-Fi (WCN6750, ath11k): join from Settings, Safari over Wi-Fi, 55–90 Mbit/s | | | Sound (speakers, main microphone), camera in Camera.app (front/rear, preview, focus, HEIC photos) | | | Data that iOS writes survives a reboot (`var_store=1 ufs_write=1`); iOS root volume on the phone's flash | | | Sileo + Procursus (dpkg, apt), tweaks, SSH | | It is a research bench, not a ROM: a session lasts a given number of seconds, then the kernel returns to the loader and hands over its log. ## Quick start: QEMU, no kernel build `prebuilt/` holds the kernel, loader and our programs built from these repositories, so all you need is the system image, which is made on your machine from Apple's IPSW. Needs: Linux x86-64, ~12 GB free disk, 4 GB free RAM. Packages (Arch): ```sh sudo pacman -S --needed git python 7zip lz4 gcc qemu-system-aarch64 qemu-ui-gtk edk2-aarch64 ``` (Debian/Ubuntu: `git python3 7zip liblz4-dev gcc qemu-system-arm qemu-efi-aarch64`; 7-Zip must be 23 or newer — it reads APFS.) ```sh git clone https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-kernel.git hackios cd hackios common/setup.sh # brings hackios-xnu-userland into the same tree, checks the host ios165/fetch.sh # downloads 7.4 GB from Apple's CDN and extracts what is needed (5-15 min) common/build.sh qemu-virt # builds the APFS images (and the kernel, if the toolchain is there) common/run.sh qemu-virt # a 20-minute session in a QEMU window ``` The lock screen appears after 2–3 minutes. - **Mouse with the left button held = finger.** Unlock / leave an app: swipe up from the very bottom edge; back: swipe from the left edge. - Keys: `H` home, `L` lock/power, `↑`/`↓` volume, `F11` (hold) five fingers. - From a script: `qemu/touch.py swipe 0.5 0.985 0.5 0.3 250`, `qemu/touch.py tap 0.615 0.71`, `qemu/touch.py key home`; screenshot: `qemu/screendump.sh shot.png`. - Right after SpringBoard appears the system is still registering apps: give it 30–40 s. - Debian/Ubuntu UEFI firmware: `QEMU_EFI=/usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_CODE.fd QEMU_VARS=/usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_VARS.fd`. ## On the phone (POCO X5 Pro 5G) You need a **POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood)** with an unlocked bootloader, `adb` and `fastboot`, and the images from the section above. Nothing is written to the phone's storage. **The phone's own firmware** is not in the repository and cannot be: it is the vendor's and is taken from the very phone it will run on, from its Android: ```sh adb pull /vendor/firmware/a660_{gmu.bin,sqe.fw,zap.mdt,zap.b00,zap.b01,zap.b02} fw-gpu/ # GPU (gpu=1) adb pull /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/wpss.{mdt,b02,b03,b04,b05,b06,b07} fw-wifi/ # Wi-Fi (wifi=1) adb pull /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/adsp.{mdt,b02,...,b36} fw-audio/ # sound (adsp=1) adb pull /vendor/firmware/aw8697_haptic.bin fw-haptic/ # haptics ``` (Put the `fw-*` directories next to the workspace. Wi-Fi also needs `fw-wifi/mac` — the radio's address on one line — and `fw-wifi/network` — network name and password. `userland/build.sh` prints which firmware went in.) ```sh common/build.sh redwood GL=1 # images + out/redwood-boot.img common/run.sh redwood 900 # loader into RAM, system image into RAM, a 15-minute session ``` or step by step with `xl`: ```sh ./xl enter # Android -> fastboot -> our loader in RAM (fastboot boot); it brings up its own USB link ./xl ramdisk # upload the system image into the phone's RAM (2.5 GB, ~80 s), once per loader session XL_SECS=900 XL_CMDLINE="touchscreen=1 cpufreq=1 bootcpu=7 cpus=8 gpu=1 wifi=1 adsp=1" ./xl run ./xl screenshot shot.png ./xl reboot # back to Android ``` `./xl` with no arguments lists every command (logs, screen and sound recording, camera frames, stop, state...). ## Prebuilt boot image Every release has `hackios-redwood-boot.img` attached: the redwood UEFI with our loader inside, ready for `fastboot boot`. It contains no Apple files; the system image is still made on your machine (above). ## Building from source `common/build.sh ` runs every step that this machine can run and uses `prebuilt/` for the rest. - **Kernel** — needs [theos](https://theos.dev/docs/installation-linux) in `~/theos` (cctools and `iPhoneOS16.5.sdk`) and `clang lld python perl`. Details: [xnu/README.md](xnu/README.md). ```sh xnu/apply.sh && xnu-deps/setup.sh && ./xnu-build.sh -j8 -k ``` - **Loader** — `xnuloader/build.sh` (clang + lld-link, an EFI application without EDK2). - **Images** — `REST=1 userland/build.sh` (variables documented at the top of that file). - **UEFI** — [uefi/README.md](uefi/README.md) (Project Silicium port); not needed to run, `prebuilt/uefi` has it. - After rebuilding: `tools/update-prebuilt.sh` refreshes `prebuilt/`. ## Porting to another device ```sh common/new-device.sh path/to/device.dtb # profile + loader platform from the phone's device tree ``` Then follow [docs/PORTING.md](docs/PORTING.md): the UEFI port, the loader's platform description, the kernel's drivers, the firmware. Device profiles live in `common/devices/` (`redwood.conf`, `qemu-virt.conf`, `_template.conf`). ## How it works ``` fastboot boot ──► UEFI (Mu-Silicium) ──► xnuloader (EFI application) │ stays resident: USB link (fastboot protocol), │ watchdog, receives the kernel's log ▼ XNU (BCM2837 config as the base + our platform) ├─ GICv3, timer, video console, return to the loader ├─ APFS (images in RAM, iOS volume on flash), ramfs (/private/var, /tmp) ├─ minicrypto instead of corecrypto, AMFI and Sandbox stand-ins (MAC policies) ├─ driver replacements: IOSurface, IOMobileFramebuffer, AppleKeyStore, network stack ├─ input: /dev/redwood-touch ◄─ Goodix GT9916 (phone) / virtio-input (QEMU) ├─ GPU: Adreno 642L, Wi-Fi: WCN6750 (ath11k via LinuxKPI), sound: ADSP / virtio-sound ▼ iOS 16.5 launchd → logd, notifyd, cfprefsd, runningboardd, backboardd, SpringBoard, apps ├─ our libraries are injected into backboardd, SpringBoard and mediaserverd │ (virtual HID services, a few ObjC method swaps — in memory only) └─ mediaserverd gets our CoreAudio output device (RedwoodAudio.driver) ``` The iOS programs, frameworks and dyld shared cache are not changed by a single byte: what they miss is done by the kernel (driver replacements) or by a library the kernel injects with `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` (`kern.exec_inject`). ## Layout | Path | What | |---|---| | `common/` | `setup.sh` (workspace), `build.sh` / `run.sh` (per device), `new-device.sh`, `devices/*.conf`, `ugit` | | `xl` | drives the phone over USB: loader, kernel runs, logs, screenshots, screen and sound recording | | `xnuloader/` | the loader: `loader.c` (UEFI application), `mkpayload.py` (kernel + images + arguments container) | | `xnu/` | our XNU changes: patch, new files, `apply.sh` / `export.sh` | | `xnu-deps/` | everything for building XNU on Linux: `setup.sh`, tool wrappers, stubs | | `xnu-build.sh`, `xnu-env.sh` | kernel build | | `uefi/`, `mkxnuimg.py` | the UEFI port and packing the boot image for `fastboot boot` | | `wifi/lx/` | the layer on which Linux's Wi-Fi driver builds for our kernel | | `qemu/` | QEMU runs, touch input, screenshots, stack symbolication | | `tools/` | recording (`recording.py`, `sound.py`), UFS/flash tools, `mk-ath11k.sh`, `new-workspace.sh`, host tests | | `prebuilt/` | built kernel, loader and UEFI pieces (`NOTICES.md` for the third-party code in the kernel) | | `docs/` | screenshots, [checks.md](docs/checks.md), [PORTING.md](docs/PORTING.md) | ## Debugging - Session log: QEMU's stdout or `logs/HHMMSS-run.log` from the phone. - `RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.tour REST=1 userland/build.sh` — an image that unlocks and opens every app of the first page. - `userabort:` in the log is the stack of a process that called `abort()`; `usertrap:` (with `systrace=1`) — crashes. - Live stacks (QEMU): `qemu/touch.py stacks NAME`, then `qemu/symstack.py LOG NAME` (needs [`ipsw`](https://github.com/blacktop/ipsw)). - How a check can lie to you: [docs/checks.md](docs/checks.md). ## Screenshots From the phone's screen, one session (`GL=1 REST=1`, `gpu=1`):

## Licenses - No iOS files are in the repositories: `ios165/fetch.sh` downloads them from Apple's CDN to your machine. - `xnu/` is a derivative work of XNU and is distributed under APSL 2.0, like XNU itself; `prebuilt/mach.*` is the kernel built from it. It also contains ath11k (BSD-3-Clause-Clear) and FreeBSD LinuxKPI code (BSD-2-Clause): see [prebuilt/NOTICES.md](prebuilt/NOTICES.md). - `xnu/files/bsd/miscfs/apfs/libzbitmap/` and `xnu-deps/build/lzbitmap/` — libzbitmap (Corellium LLC, MIT here); `xnu/files/bsd/miscfs/apfs/libdeflate/` — libdeflate 1.24 (Eric Biggers, MIT, `COPYING` there). - ath11k, Linux and FreeBSD sources are not in the repository: `tools/mk-ath11k.sh` fetches pinned releases. `wifi/lx/patches/*.patch` are our changes to FreeBSD headers; the rest of `wifi/lx/` is ours. - `uefi/files/Binaries/redwood` and `prebuilt/uefi/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd` contain UEFI drivers from the phone's Xiaomi firmware, distributed the way Project Silicium distributes them for other devices; `prebuilt/uefi/mkbootimg.py` — AOSP, Apache-2.0. - This repository is licensed under the [Apple Public Source License 2.0](LICENSE): our changes to XNU are a derivative of XNU and must be, and our other code here (loader, scripts) is released under the same license. Third-party code keeps its own license, as listed above. ## Team OOSEX GANG — [@oodze](https://t.me/oodze) (founder), [@netusd](https://t.me/netusd), [@wannqn](https://t.me/wannqn), [@hxfuxyyXD](https://t.me/hxfuxyyXD). High-performance Roblox aimbot focused on adaptive smooth tracking and precise auto aim.  
Clean modular Lua structure, fully configurable and compatible with most popular executors.

---

## 🎯 What it is

**Roblox Aimbot** is a client-side script that provides adaptive auto aim and smooth target tracking.  
It is designed to be lightweight, easy to configure and work with the majority of modern executors.

> ⚠️  
> Use at your own risk. This is an open-source educational project.

- Aim smoothness  
- FOV size  
- Target priority  
- Team check

- Hotkeys

## ❓ FAQ

It is tested with the most popular ones. Compatibility may vary.

No. Fully open and free.

Yes — everything is configurable in the UI or config file.

---

## 🤝 Contributing

Pull requests, bug reports and improvements are welcome.

---

---

# php2shell-scanner

A command-line tool for detecting CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in PHP applications.

## How It Works

The scanner sends a minimal multipart control request followed by up to three crafted multipart probes. The probes use PHP array keys nested 62 levels deep and increase from 1 MiB to 20 MiB, matching the detection logic used by Assetnote's internal scanner.

A target is reported vulnerable when the probe produces a PHP memory-exhaustion error, a differential empty HTTP 500, a PHP-FPM worker failure, or an advertised PHP version known to be unpatched. Initial 5xx responses, common request-rejection statuses, and nonempty HTTP 500 responses without the PHP fatal-error signature are not treated as crash signals.

The scanner tests `/index.php` by default. A path supplied in the URL is preserved, and `--path` or `--path-file` can test custom paths. phpMyAdmin targets are automatically retested at `/show_config_errors.php`. Redirects are not followed.

### SAPI Modes

The default `--sapi auto` mode applies both mod_php and PHP-FPM verdict rules, matching the combined behavior of Assetnote's postmodules. Use `--sapi mod_php` or `--sapi fpm` to restrict detection to a known SAPI.

### Network Impact

Each tested path may receive a 42-byte control request and three probes totalling about 29 MiB. Probing stops as soon as the verdict is settled, and duplicate input URLs are scanned once.

## Requirements

- Python 3.9+
- h11
- tqdm

## Installation

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Usage

Scan a single host:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com
```

Scan a list of hosts:

```
python3 scanner.py -l hosts.txt
```

Scan with multiple threads and save results:

```
python3 scanner.py -l hosts.txt -t 20 -o results.json
```

Scan with custom headers:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com -H "Authorization: Bearer token" -H "Cookie: session=abc"
```

Scan a custom path:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --path /phpinfo.php
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --path /index.php --path /admin.php
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --path-file paths.txt
```

Use only PHP-FPM verdict rules:

```
python3 scanner.py -u https://example.com --sapi fpm
```

## Options

```
-u, --url         Single URL to check
-l, --list        File containing hosts (one per line)
-t, --threads     Number of concurrent threads (default: 10)
--timeout         Request timeout in seconds (default: 60)
-o, --output      Output file for results (JSON)
--all-results     Save all results, not just vulnerable hosts
-k, --insecure    Disable TLS certificate verification
-H, --header      Custom header (can be used multiple times)
-v, --verbose     Show verdict reasons and response snippets
-q, --quiet       Only output vulnerable hosts
--no-color        Disable colored output
--sapi            Verdict rules: auto, mod_php, or fpm (default: auto)
--path            Custom path to test (can be used multiple times)
--path-file       File containing paths to test (one per line)
```

## Credits

The first, original discovery of php2shell is attributed to the Calif team. You can read their write up here: [https://calif.io/php2shell/](https://calif.io/php2shell/).

The scanner was built by the Assetnote Security Research Team using logic built for [Searchlight's Exposure Platform](https://www.slcyber.io/exposure).

## Output

Results are printed to the terminal. When using `-o`, vulnerable hosts are saved to a JSON file with the verdict reason and redacted HTTP request/response evidence.

## Limitations

On specific PHP configurations, the scanner may report a false positive when its multipart probe exceeds PHP's `memory_limit`. Patched and vulnerable versions can then return the same empty HTTP 500 response.

This was reproduced on patched PHP 8.4.27 with `memory_limit` values from **2M to 32M**, and on PHP 8.3.36 at **128M** when `max_multipart_body_parts` is set to **2785 or higher**. The exact threshold may vary between builds.

When PHP does not disclose its version, the scanner cannot distinguish this safe post-patch OOM from the vulnerable pre-patch behavior. Results should therefore be verified against the installed PHP version and any vendor backports

items.description: Turn any SVG into a professional 60 fps animation. A Claude Code skill that brings anything drawn to life: live faces, full-body acting and whole scenes, in React Native and SwiftUI.
items.readme: # Motion For Anything You Draw For designers and engineers who want to bring their apps and drawings to life. Making a drawing move is easy. Making it feel alive is hard: it has to breathe, look around, blink, shift its weight and act, without ever freezing or jumping. This skill helps your agent get there. It started as the method I used to bring the illustrations in my app to life, and grew into a way to animate anything drawn: characters and creatures, plants, cloth, fire, smoke, water, weather, lights, machines, icons, logos, charts and whole scenes. The animation above is drawn and animated entirely in code, with the templates in this repo. ## Install ```bash npx skills@latest add rossark0/rossark-motion-skill ``` ## Why use it? Agents don't animate like animators. Ask an agent to bring a character to life and it will often swap one drawing for another, so the face teleports from one expression to the next. It moves through each pose with its own eased tween, so the body stops dead at every pose. Everything moves in sync, like a machine. Blinks are so short they flicker, everything bounces, and a thin line shows across the face where two shapes meet. All these small things add up, and the result looks like a slideshow instead of something alive. This skill lists those mistakes and how to fix them: one clock for the whole scene, parts that turn around their real pivots, trailing parts that follow a beat later, idle life that never stops, smooth paths through key poses, small amplitudes and strong curves. When you have a reference video, it measures the motion frame by frame before building, because what makes a reference feel alive is often too small to see. For motion in an interface, it follows [Emil Kowalski's](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills) rules and Benji Taylor's [Family values](https://benji.org/family-values). ## Reference - **[SKILL.md](./SKILL.md)**: The skill. Principles, recipes for every kind of subject, live faces, full-body acting, scenes that tell an action, motion in an interface, pitfalls, working from a reference video, and a workflow. - **[MOTION.md](./MOTION.md)**: A notes file for your project. Copy it next to your art and fill in Part 2 as you go: where the code is, your rules, what your art can't do, and how you check changes. The skill reads it first. - **[motion.ts](./templates/react-native/motion.ts)** and **[Motion.swift](./templates/swiftui/Motion.swift)**: The engine, for React Native and SwiftUI. Loop and one-shot clocks, `track`, `flow` (smooth acting through key poses), `seg`, `wave`, `loop`, `bell`, `seeded` and the curves. - **[liveFace.tsx](./templates/react-native/liveFace.tsx)** and **[LiveFace.swift](./templates/swiftui/LiveFace.swift)**: Live eyes and mouths that glide, blink and smile. You give them the geometry and the colours. - **[sheet.sh](./tools/sheet.sh)**: Contact sheets of a video at its full frame rate, to study timing or check your own render. - **[track_edges.py](./tools/track_edges.py)**: Measures a subject's edges frame by frame, to catch motion too small for the eye: a 2% jiggle, a float, a sway. - **[sample_colors.py](./tools/sample_colors.py)**: Reads exact colours from a video frame. - **[demo/](./demo)**: The scenes on this page, a phone frame and an offline renderer that turns them into MP4 and GIF. ## Demos **Reveal** ([source](demo/RevealScene.swift), [MP4](demo/reveal.mp4)), at the top of this page. Full-body acting in a phone frame, on one clock, in a 9-second loop at 60 fps: - a mystery silhouette floats in, its feet hanging limp, its shadow breathing with the height; - the kid hovers, falls with gravity, squashes on landing and keeps the volume; - poses flow into each other with `flow`, idle life never stops, and the head and forearms follow through; - a ball rolls in from off screen, the eyes follow it, the kick hits at the middle of the swing, and the ball flies off spinning; then the kid turns to you and waves; - a toy-like build seen from a little above: a big head, a short torso, round shoes and a wide oval shadow. **Garden** ([source](demo/GardenScene.swift), [MP4](demo/garden.mp4)), a 10-second loop: - she pulls the can back, then pours: drops fall in seeded arcs with gravity and the soil darkens as it gets wet; - the stem grows in two pushes, the leaves unfurl one after another, and the petals open one by one with a small twist; - a butterfly wanders in from off screen and lands, the stem dips under its weight, and her head and eyes track it all the way; - she grins and hops, with her pigtails, hat and can trailing the motion; then the petals drift down and the plant settles back into the sprout. **Chef** ([source](demo/ChefScene.swift), [MP4](demo/chef.mp4)), a 9.6-second loop: - steam rises from the pan, the flame flickers on two waves, and the burner knob turns up before each flip; - the first flip: knees dip, the pancake turns in the air under gravity, his eyes follow it and his head a beat later, and it lands with a squash; - the second flip goes too high: surprise, it lands on his hat, the hat squashes and wobbles, the pancake slides off and he catches it with the pan; - contact stays exact: every throw starts and ends where the pan or the hat really is, and the hand is solved onto the handle. **Orbit** ([source](demo/OrbitScene.swift), [MP4](demo/orbit.mp4)): - a ring of cards orbiting in depth: the fronts in front of the bird, the backs behind it, edge-on at the sides; - the bird floats and tilts, its wings flutter, and its feet and tufts follow through; - sparkles that appear and disappear once per loop, at seeded times. To render them again on macOS 14+: ```bash swiftc -parse-as-library -target arm64-apple-macos14 \ templates/swiftui/Motion.swift templates/swiftui/LiveFace.swift demo/*.swift -o /tmp/render-demo /tmp/render-demo reveal /tmp/frames phone fps=60 # or: garden, chef, orbit ffmpeg -framerate 60 -i /tmp/frames/%04d.png -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 20 demo/reveal.mp4 ```

# HackiOS — userland

The user-space half of **HackiOS**: Apple's open-source XNU kernel on Android phone hardware (POCO X5 Pro 5G) and in
QEMU, running the unmodified iOS 16.5 user space. The kernel, loader, UEFI and the `common/` scripts are in
[hackios-xnu-kernel](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-kernel) — **start there**.

> **No Apple files are in this repository.** `ios165/fetch.sh` downloads the iOS 16.5 IPSW from Apple's CDN to your
> machine and extracts what is needed there. HackiOS is an independent research project by OOSEX GANG and is not
> affiliated with, authorised or endorsed by Apple Inc.

## Getting it

The two repositories are built as one tree. Clone the kernel repository and let it bring this one in:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-kernel.git hackios
cd hackios
common/setup.sh        # checks this repository out into the same directory (git dir .userland.git)
common/ugit status     # git for this repository inside that tree
```

## What is here

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `userland/build.sh` | builds the APFS images: `root.apfs` (our init, libraries, launchd jobs, firmware) and `system.apfs` (the selected part of iOS 16.5 and its cryptexes); every option is documented at the top |
| `userland/src/` | `init.c` (process 1), injected libraries (`inject.c` backboardd, `inject_sb.c` SpringBoard, `inject_media.c` mediaserverd, `inject_tweaks.c`), the CoreAudio output device (`audio_plugin.c`), the OpenGL ES bridge to Mesa (`eagl.c`), Metal driver work, tests |
| `userland/libmini/` | a tiny libc for the static programs |
| `userland/rc.*`, `com.redwood.*.plist` | job lists and launchd jobs for test scenarios (`RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.tour`, `rc.jobs.ssh`, ...) |
| `userland/mkjobs.py`, `jobinfo.py` | the stock iOS launchd jobs: which are loaded, who provides a Mach service |
| `userland/var/` | our default preferences for `/private/var` |
| `ios165/` | `fetch.sh` / `fetch-from-ipsw.py` (take iOS out of the IPSW), `select-system.py` (what goes into the image) |
| `tools/apfs/` | APFS on the computer: `mkapfs.py` (image writer), reader, checks, write tests |
| `tools/mk-mesa.sh`, `tools/mesa/` | Mesa 25.0.7 with our patches: freedreno on Darwin, the AIR (Metal IR) frontend |
| `tools/air/`, `tools/metal/`, `tools/metallib.py` | Metal shader (AIR) checks and analysis; notes in `docs/air.md` |
| `tools/mk-jb.sh`, `jb-preinstall.py` | Procursus bootstrap + Sileo for the package manager prefix |
| `tools/font_trim.py` | trims two oversized iOS fonts so the image fits |
| `prebuilt/userland/` | our programs and libraries, built — used when there is no cross toolchain |

## Building the images

```sh
ios165/fetch.sh               # once
REST=1 userland/build.sh      # -> userland/root.apfs, userland/system.apfs
GL=1 REST=1 userland/build.sh # with OpenGL ES (Mesa) for the window server; on the phone with gpu=1
```

Without the cross toolchain (theos + iPhoneOS16.5.sdk, see the kernel repository) the build takes our programs from
`prebuilt/userland`; with it, it compiles `userland/src`.

A job list (`RC_JOBS=file`) is run by our `init`, not by a shell: iOS 16.5's root has no shell, lines are split on
blanks, there is no quoting and no variable assignment; only `>> FILE` and a trailing `&` are understood.

## Licenses

Our code in this repository is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Mesa (MIT) is not in the
repository: `tools/mk-mesa.sh` fetches release 25.0.7, `tools/mesa/*.patch` are our changes to it. apfsprogs
(GPL-2.0) is not in the repository either: `tools/apfs/check-image.sh` fetches and builds only `apfsck`.

It is used for coding, agent workflows, reasoning and bilingual Chinese/English tasks. Teams choose GLM models when they want a capable agent model at a lower cost than the largest frontier models. GLM 5.3 is a good fit for: - coding agents and tool-using workflows; - repository-scale instructions and `AGENTS.md` files; - bilingual products; - cost-sensitive batch jobs; - teams that want a non-US model family in their routing mix. Get the key and base URL Create an account at **[7api.st](https://7api.st/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=glm-5.3-abliterated)**. Copy the API key and the Base URL from the dashboard. ```bash export SEVEN_API_KEY="sk-..." export SEVEN_API_BASE_URL="https://.../v1" ``` ### 2. Confirm the GLM 5.3 model ID Open the dashboard and copy the exact ID for the GLM 5.3 variant you want — standard, abliterated or uncensored. Availability changes; the dashboard is the source of truth. ### 3. OpenAI-compatible request ```python import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ["SEVEN_API_KEY"], base_url=os.environ["SEVEN_API_BASE_URL"], ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model="GLM_5_3_MODEL_ID", # copy from the dashboard messages=[ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a precise coding assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Refactor this function and explain the trade-offs: ..."}, ], ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` ### 4. # rom

Python CLI to find and download ROMs, ISOs and Switch games from the terminal.
It has an interactive UI (Textual) like `epub-search`, name search, downloads with
a progress bar, and a folder organised by platform.

> English-language version of the original Portuguese project by
> [sostenesapollo](https://github.com/sostenesapollo/rom-cli). Thanks to the
> original author for the base work — this fork translates the interface and
> docs to English and tracks the upstream fixes.

## Requirements

- Python 3.8+
- macOS or Linux
- `textual` (`install.sh` installs it into its own venv)

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/danisiber/rom-cli.git
cd rom-cli
./install.sh
```

This creates a venv in `~/.venvs/rom`, installs `textual`, and publishes `rom`
(and `rom-remote`) into `~/bin`. Use `PREFIX=/usr/local ./install.sh` for a
different destination.

## Usage

```bash
rom                          # opens the platform picker and browses
rom -p switch                # opens straight into the Switch catalog
rom -p switchports           # only the Switch ports/homebrew
rom "metroid"                # searches every source
rom -y -p gba "pokemon"      # downloads the best match without asking
rom --list "metroid"         # lists only, does not download
rom --print-url -p switch …  # prints the direct link (aria2/curl)
rom -l                       # lists the platforms
rom --index                  # builds/prints the catalog index
rom --refresh                # rebuilds the index (ignores the cache)
```

With no query, `rom` opens the **platform picker**; once you pick one, it lists
that platform's whole catalog (pages of 300, `n`/`b` to move) — so you can
browse without typing anything. Typing in the field and pressing `Enter` goes
back to searching.

In the UI: `↑↓` navigate, `space` mark, `d` download (the marked ones or the
current one), `p` switch platform, `n`/`b` page, `ctrl+b` options palette,
`ctrl+a` select all, `ctrl+n` clear, `q` quit.

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-p, --platform` | platform (switch, snes, gba, ps2, nds, wii…) |
| `-y, --yes` | download the best match without the menu |
| `--list` | list only |
| `--print-url` | resolve and print the direct link only |
| `--refresh` | rebuild the catalog index |
| `--index` | download/print the index and exit |
| `-n, --number` | how many results to show (default 15) |
| `-o, --out` | destination folder (default `~/Downloads/roms` or `$ROM_DIR`) |
| `-l, --platforms` | list platforms |

Platforms: `switch`, `switchports`, `ps5`, `ps4`, `ps3`, `psv`, `ps2`, `ps1`,
`psp`, `nds`, `gba`, `snes`, `pc`, `nes`, `gb`, `gbc`, `n64`, `3ds`, `gc`, `wii`,
`genesis`, `mastersystem`, `dreamcast`, `saturn`, `arcade`.

Files go to `~/Downloads/roms/<platform>/`.

## How it works

- **Switch**: the dlarchive index (`files_api.php`). The nsp-roms page embeds
  links with a token that expires; here `rom` resolves through the index and
  grabs a direct, token-free URL. It also works for NDS, GBA, SNES and PC.
- **Switch ports**: the `switchports` platform merges two sources — the dlarchive
  catalog and an Archive.org scan (`switch port` / `homebrew port` / `nsp`+`port`),
  with a 7-day cache. Around 35 ports (GTA, Halo, Simpsons Hit & Run, SM64 NX,
  Twilight Princess, Cave Story, Pizza Tower, Max Payne, Hello Neighbor, Diablo...).
- **PS3 and PS Vita**: NoPayStation — downloads `.pkg` straight from Sony's CDN
  (`zeus.dl.playstation.net`), no token needed.
- **PS2, PS1 and PSP**: RomsGames (search + a POST that returns the file).
- **PS4 and PS5**: dlpsgame (search via WP REST). The direct download works when
  the post links a supported host (mediafire, Google Drive, 1fichier); when it
  doesn't, `rom` shows the page so you can grab the link yourself.
- **Best sellers first**: while browsing a platform, the best-selling titles
  (Wikipedia lists, 30-day cache) come first with ★; the rest follow alphabetically.
  Platforms without a full listing (PS4/PS5) are browsed through that best-seller
  list itself.
- **Fallback**: Archive.org on platforms with a thin catalogue.
- The catalog index is cached (`~/.cache/rom-cli/dlarchive.json`, 12h TTL) —
  which makes searches instant. `--refresh` rebuilds it.
- Ranking is by title match, with a penalty for hacks/translations/betas and a
  preference for `Base` over `Update`/`DLC`.
- Files are validated before being written (zip, 7z, `PFS0` for `.nsp`, and
  `PKG`/`CNT` for `.pkg`).
- Downloads are resumable (`.part` + `Range`).

## Remote mode (`rom-remote`)

Runs on the Mac worker (`ssh mac`) and brings the files back. Useful when this
Mac's network blocks the download hosts.

```bash
rom-remote -p switch "mario kart"    # opens the UI on the worker
rom-remote -y -p snes "metroid"      # downloads there and syncs back here
```

Tune it with `ROM_REMOTE_HOST`, `ROM_REMOTE_DIR` and `ROM_DIR`.

## Notice

Only use what you have the right to.

--- ## 🧭 Table of Contents - [Overview](#-overview) - [What is a YouTube Viewer Bot?](#-what-is-a-youtube-viewer-bot) - [Key Features](#-key-features) - [The Problem](#-the-problem) - [The Solution](#-the-solution) - [Quick Start](#-quick-start) - [Module Catalog](#-module-catalog) - [Session & Proxy Management](#-session--proxy-management) - [Retention & Watch-Time Engine](#-retention--watch-time-engine) - [System Requirements](#-system-requirements) - [Installation](#-installation) - [AI Integration (2026)](#-ai-integration-2026) - [How It Works](#-how-it-works) - [Comparison](#-comparison) - [Known Issues](#-known-issues) - [Changelog](#-changelog) - [FAQ](#-faq) - [Community & Support](#-community--support) --- ## 📊 Overview | Category | Details | |---|---| | **Product type** | Windows desktop application (compiled `.exe`) | | **Purpose** | Automated YouTube view generation with retention simulation | | **Primary interface** | GUI dashboard + headless batch mode | | **Concurrency model** | Session-pool based, proxy-rotated | | **Watch-time engine** | Per-session timeline scripting with drift correction | | **Proxy support** | HTTP, SOCKS4, SOCKS5, residential, mobile | | **Data persistence** | Local SQLite job store, encrypted credential vault | | **Distribution** | Direct download from project landing page | The `yt-view-bot` application is a session-orchestration framework built specifically for YouTube view and watch-time automation. It manages pools of browser sessions, rotates proxy identities, and scripts realistic playback timelines (including seek, pause, and skip events) to reproduce the watch patterns a genuine viewer produces. Everything runs locally from a single `.exe` — no runtime installs, no Python environment, no dependency chain. --- ## 🤖 What is a YouTube Viewer bot? | Term | Explanation | |---|---| | **Session** | An isolated browser profile (cookies, UA, viewport, fingerprint) representing one synthetic viewer | | **Proxy pool** | Rotating set of IP endpoints assigned per-session so views don't share an origin | | **Retention script** | A timeline of play/pause/seek actions that mimics human watch behavior | | **Drift** | The gap between wall-clock playback time and scripted timeline position; corrected periodically | | **View-count boundary** | The threshold at which YouTube may freeze or filter counts; the bot throttles to stay under it | | **Fingerprint** | Composite of canvas hash, WebGL renderer, fonts, timezone, and UA sent to YouTube | | **Job** | One configured run — N sessions, M views, one target video, one proxy pool | The bot is not a "click play N times" loop. It manages the full identity of each session — fingerprint, cookie jar, and proxy binding are locked together at spawn time and cannot drift mid-run. This matters because YouTube's view validation checks consistency between IP, cookie state, and playback telemetry. --- ## 🎯 Key Features | Feature | Description | Benefit | |---|---|---| | **Fingerprint locking** | Canvas/WebGL/UA/fonts sampled once and reused per session | Views don't get grouped as one synthetic actor | | **Proxy rotation modes** | Round-robin, sticky, per-session, per-job | Fine control over IP exposure for a target video | | **Retention scripting** | Timeline JSON with play, pause, seek, skip, mute | Watch-time looks organic instead of a 100% full play | | **Drift correction** | Re-syncs timeline against actual `currentTime` every 4s | Prevents runaway desync on slow proxies | | **Headless batch mode** | CLI flag runs jobs without GUI | Schedulable via Windows Task Scheduler | | **Per-job concurrency cap** | Limits simultaneous sessions (default 3) | Reduces proxy burn and detection surface | | **Encrypted vault** | AES-encrypted proxy creds and cookie jars at rest | No plaintext credentials on disk | | **Live telemetry panel** | Real-time view-count delta, session health, proxy latency | You see failures before the job finishes | | **Resume-after-crash** | Job state persisted to SQLite; resume from last completed session | Long jobs survive reboots | | **Warm-up mode** | Sessions browse homepage/related videos for 30–90s before target | Reduces "instant-jump" signal | | **AI retention profiles (2026)** | Model picks realistic watch percentages per video length | Randomized retention that follows real audience curves | | **AI proxy health scorer (2026)** | Scores proxies by failure rate and latency trend | Skips dying proxies before they burn a session | --- ## 🧨 The Problem - Manual view farms get flagged because every session shares one IP or one UA string. - Naive bots play 100% of the video every time — retention curves look artificial and views get filtered. - Proxy pools silently degrade: you only discover a dead proxy after a session fails to register a view. - Playback timers drift on slow connections, so a "watch 4:30" script actually delivers 3:12 or 6:40 of watch time. - Long jobs crash mid-run and there's no resume — you start the whole thing over. - Fingerprint mismatch (IP in one country, timezone in another) is a top cause of dropped views. - No visibility into *why* views didn't count — you get a number and nothing else. --- ## 🛠️ The Solution | Problem | Solution | |---|---| | Shared IP/UA across sessions | Per-session proxy binding + locked fingerprint at spawn | | Artificial 100% retention | Retention timeline scripting with random pause/seek events | | Dead proxies discovered late | AI proxy health scorer pre-filters failing endpoints | | Playback timer drift | 4-second drift correction against actual `currentTime` | | No crash recovery | SQLite job state + resume-from-last-session | | Fingerprint mismatch | Geo-consistent fingerprint assembly (timezone ← proxy region) | | Zero failure diagnostics | Per-session log with failure reason (proxy fail, view filtered, playback error) | --- ## 🚀 Quick Start 1. 🧾 **Visit the project page** and hit the download section — you get a zip containing the `.exe` and a `config/` folder. 2. 📦 **Extract** the zip to a folder you own (not `Program Files` — the app writes job state next to itself). 3. ▶️ **Run the .exe** — first launch creates `config/settings.json` and an empty proxy pool. 4. 🧩 **Load your proxy list** in the Proxy Manager tab (one `host:port:user:pass` per line, protocol dropdown per pool). 5. 🎬 **Create a job** — paste the target video URL, set view count, sessions, and pick a retention profile. Hit Start.
> First run will ask you to accept a one-time notice about YouTube ToS and local data storage. Nothing is sent anywhere except the YouTube requests themselves. --- ## 🧩 Module Catalog 44 modules across nine subsystems. Status reflects the current 2026 build. | Module | Status | Description | |---|---|---| | `SessionSpawner` | ✅ Working | Creates isolated browser profiles with locked fingerprint | | `FingerprintSampler` | ✅ Working | Captures canvas, WebGL, fonts, UA, timezone per session | | `GeoResolver` | ✅ Working | Matches timezone/locale to proxy region | | `CookieJarManager` | ✅ Working | Encrypted per-session cookie persistence | | `ProxyPool` | ✅ Working | Pool container with health state per endpoint | | `ProxyRotator` | ✅ Working | Round-robin / sticky / per-job rotation strategies | | `ProxyHealthScorer` | ✅ Working | AI-scored endpoint reliability (2026) | | `ProxyImportParser` | ✅ Working | Parses `host:port:user:pass` and URI formats | | `RetentionScripter` | ✅ Working | Builds play/pause/seek timeline from profile | | `RetentionProfiles` | ✅ Working | Named retention templates (short, medium, long-form) | | `DriftCorrector` | ✅ Working | 4s re-sync against actual player `currentTime` | | `PlaybackController` | ✅ Working | Play, pause, seek, mute, skip events | | `WarmUpWalker` | ✅ Working | Pre-target homepage/related browsing | | `ViewCounter` | ✅ Working | Tracks accepted view deltas from telemetry | | `ThrottleGuard` | ✅ Working | Caps concurrent sessions per job | | `JobScheduler` | ✅ Working | Queue and run multiple jobs sequentially | | `JobStore` | ✅ Working | SQLite persistence of job + session state | | `ResumeEngine` | ✅ Working | Resume crashed job from last completed session | | `HeadlessRunner` | ✅ Working | CLI batch execution without GUI | | `CredentialVault` | ✅ Working | AES-encrypted storage for proxy creds | | `ConfigManager` | ✅ Working | `settings.json` load/validate/migrate | | `LogRotator` | ✅ Working | Rotates session logs by size/date | | `SessionLogger` | ✅ Working | Per-session event log with failure reason | | `TelemetryPanel` | ✅ Working | Live view delta, session health, proxy latency | | `LatencyMonitor` | ✅ Working | Per-proxy RTT sampling | | `FailureClassifier` | ✅ Working | Tags failures: proxy, playback, filtered, timeout | | `AiRetentionPicker` | ✅ Working | Model selects retention % from video length | | `AiProxyAdvisor` | ✅ Working | Recommends pool swaps mid-job | | `FingerprintConsistencyCheck` | ✅ Working | Flags IP/geo/UA mismatch before spawn | | `SessionPoolRecycler` | ✅ Working | Recycles dead or flagged sessions | | `RateLimiter` | ✅ Working | Per-proxy request pacing | | `UAProfileLibrary` | ✅ Working | Curated UA + viewport pairs per browser family | | `CookieSeeder` | ✅ Working | Seeds sessions with plausible prior activity | | `VideoResolver` | ✅ Working | Resolves video ID from URL variants / shorts | | `PlaylistWalker` | ✅ Working | Handles playlist and related-video targets | | `DwellTimer` | ✅ Working | Adds non-playback dwell time on the watch page | | `MuteRandomizer` | ✅ Working | Randomized mute/unmute during playback | | `QualitySwitcher` | ✅ Working | Random quality selection per session | | `AdSkipper` | ✅ Working | Handles pre-roll skip timing | | `StatsAggregator` | ✅ Working | Post-job stats: views, filtered, failed, avg watch | | `ExportModule` | ✅ Working | Exports job stats to CSV | | `UpdateChecker` | ✅ Working | Checks landing page for newer build | | `DiagnosticsBundle` | ⚠️ Beta | One-click zip of logs + config for support | | `ProxyAutoRefill` | ⚠️ Beta | Pulls replacement proxies from configured provider | --- ## 🕸️ Session & Proxy Management **Session isolation** — each session is a fully separate browser profile on disk under `sessions/`. Cookie jar, fingerprint, and proxy binding are written at spawn and never mutated. **Proxy binding rules** - `sticky`: one proxy → one session for the job's lifetime - `round-robin`: proxies cycle every N sessions (configurable) - `per-job`: one proxy pool per job, isolated from other jobs - `pool-shuffle`: reshuffles the pool every 10 sessions **Health scoring** — the `ProxyHealthScorer` tracks failures, timeouts, and latency trend per endpoint. Proxies below the threshold are quarantined rather than deleted, so you can inspect why they failed. **Fingerprint assembly order** — proxy region → timezone → locale → UA family → viewport → canvas/WebGL. Each value depends on the previous, which is why you can't just randomize the UA independently. --- ## ⏱️ Retention & Watch-Time Engine The retention engine is what separates a working bot from a view-filtered one. A fixed "watch 100%" pattern is the single most common cause of dropped views. **Timeline format** (retention profile) ``` { "name": "medium-random", "watch_pct": [0.45, 0.92], "events": [ { "at": 0.12, "action": "pause", "duration": [3, 9] }, { "at": 0.40, "action": "seek", "delta": [-8, 8] }, { "at": 0.70, "action": "mute", "duration": [5, 20] } ] } ``` `watch_pct` is a range — each session samples a random value inside it. `AiRetentionPicker` overrides this range per video using length-aware curves (short videos skew higher, long-form skews lower and more variable). **Drift correction** — every 4 seconds the engine compares the scripted timeline position to the actual `currentTime` from the player. If drift exceeds 2.5 seconds, the script re-anchors. Without this, slow proxies push the timeline out of sync and the session "watches" the wrong segment. --- ## 🖥️ System Requirements | Component | Minimum | Recommended | |---|---|---| | **OS** | Windows 10 64-bit (build 1909+) | Windows 11 23H2+ | | **CPU** | 4 cores / 4 threads | 8 cores / 16 threads | | **RAM** | 8 GB | 16 GB (16+ sessions concurrent) | | **Disk** | 2 GB free | 8 GB free (session profile cache) | | **Network** | 10 Mbps down | 50 Mbps down, low jitter | | **Proxy pool** | 1 endpoint per concurrent session | 5–10 endpoints per concurrent session | | **Display** | 1280×720 | 1920×1080 | | **Admin rights** | Not required | Not required | | **Runtime** | None (self-contained) | None | **Tips for best results** - Keep concurrent sessions at 3 or below for a single target video — the throttle guard defaults to this for a reason. - Use residential or mobile proxies for the target video; datacenter proxies are the fastest route to filtered views. - Warm up sessions (`WarmUpWalker`) — sessions that jump straight to a target video behave differently than ones that browse first. - Don't point two jobs at the same video simultaneously; the view counter aggregates per video and you'll lose track of which job contributed what. - Keep at least 5 proxies beyond your concurrency cap so the health scorer has room to quarantine without starving the pool. - Run headless batch mode from Task Scheduler if you want overnight jobs; the GUI adds ~15% CPU per session. --- ## 📥 Installation 1. **Download the build.** Go to the project landing page, download the current zip. The archive contains the `.exe`, a `config/` skeleton, and a short `readme-first.txt`. 2. **Extract to a writable folder.** The app writes `jobs.db`, `sessions/`, and `logs/` next to the executable. Avoid `Program Files` and any path with non-ASCII characters. 3. **Run the .exe.** First launch runs a config check, creates defaults, and opens the dashboard. If Windows SmartScreen prompts, choose "More info → Run anyway" — the build is unsigned. 4. **Configure proxies.** Open the Proxy Manager tab, paste your list, pick the protocol per pool, and hit Validate. Anything red is dead on arrival. 5. **Create your first job.** Target video URL, view count, sessions, retention profile. Start small (5 views) to confirm the pipeline works end-to-end before scaling up. --- ## 🧠 AI Integration (2026) Three AI-assisted subsystems are active in this build. None of them send your data to a remote model — the models are small, local, and shipped inside the `.exe`. **`AiRetentionPicker`** — Instead of a fixed watch-percentage range, this picks a retention value from a distribution fit against real audience retention curves for the video's length category. A 3-minute video might sample 70–95%; a 40-minute video samples 18–55% with more variance. This is the single biggest improvement over fixed-range retention. **`AiProxyAdvisor`** — Samples proxy latency and failure rates mid-job, and when a pool's health drops below threshold it suggests (or auto-applies, if enabled) a pool swap. It also flags proxies that *respond* fine but consistently fail to register views — a failure mode latency monitoring misses. **`FailureClassifier`** — Post-job, classifies each failed session into proxy failure, playback error, filtered view, or timeout. This replaces the old "count of failures" with a breakdown you can actually act on. Real-time updates are also new: the telemetry panel now streams view-delta and session health over a local WebSocket instead of polling every 5 seconds, so a dying proxy shows up within ~1 second. --- ## 🏗️ How It Works The application is a session-orchestration pipeline. When you start a job, the `JobScheduler` asks the `SessionSpawner` for N sessions. The spawner pulls endpoints from the `ProxyPool`, runs each through `FingerprintConsistencyCheck`, then builds a browser profile via `FingerprintSampler` and `GeoResolver` — timezone and locale are derived from the proxy's geolocation, not randomized independently. If the consistency check fails (proxy says Germany, fingerprint says Vietnam), the session is rejected before it ever touches YouTube. Once a session is live, `WarmUpWalker` optionally browses the homepage and a couple of related videos for 30–90 seconds. Then `VideoResolver` turns your target URL into a video ID, `PlaybackController` navigates to the watch page, and `RetentionScripter` builds the timeline from the selected profile (or from `AiRetentionPicker` if AI mode is on). `PlaybackController` executes the timeline, while `DriftCorrector` samples `currentTime` every 4 seconds and re-anchors if the script has drifted. `DwellTimer`, `MuteRandomizer`, and `QualitySwitcher` layer on the smaller behavioral details. `ViewCounter` reads the view-count delta from the watch page after the session ends, and `FailureClassifier` tags any session that didn't produce a delta. Job state is written to SQLite after each completed session by `JobStore`, which is what makes `ResumeEngine` work — a crash at session 47 of 200 resumes at session 47, not session 1. `StatsAggregator` produces the end-of-job summary and `ExportModule` writes it to CSV if you want the data elsewhere. --- ## ⚖️ Comparison | Aspect | Generic view bots | Browser-extension "viewers" | `yt-view-bot` | |---|---|---|---| | Session isolation | Shared browser profile | Runs in your real browser | One profile per session, locked | | Proxy handling | Manual, one IP | None | Pool with health scoring + rotation | | Retention realism | Fixed 100% play | Whatever you do manually | Scripted timeline + AI curve sampling | | Drift handling | None | N/A | 4s re-sync against `currentTime` | | Crash recovery | Restart from zero | N/A | Resume from last completed session | | Failure diagnostics | Count only | N/A | Classified per session | | Batch scheduling | Manual | N/A | Headless CLI + Task Scheduler | | Fingerprint consistency | Random UA | Your real fingerprint | Geo-consistent assembly | Fair framing: the extension route is genuinely simpler if you just want a handful of views from your own browser — this tool is for people running hundreds of sessions and needing them to look separate. Generic bots are fine for targets that don't validate hard; this one is built for the ones that do. --- ## 🧯 Known Issues | Issue | Solution | |---|---| | Views register but get filtered after ~48h | Retention profile too uniform — switch to `AiRetentionPicker` and raise `watch_pct` variance | | Session hangs on watch page with no playback | Usually a dead proxy that passes latency check but fails media requests; quarantine it manually | | `DiagnosticsBundle` sometimes omits the last session log | Known beta issue — the log flush races the bundle build; wait 5s after job end before bundling | | High RAM usage above 12 concurrent sessions | Expected — each session holds a browser profile in memory; drop concurrency or raise RAM | | Proxy validation passes but spawn fails | Fingerprint consistency check rejecting geo mismatch; loosen the check or fix proxy region metadata | | Headless mode won't pick up config changes | Config is loaded once at process start; restart the headless process after editing `settings.json` | --- ## 📜 Changelog | Version | Date | Changes | |---|---|---| | 2026.3 | 2026-03-18 | `AiProxyAdvisor` auto-apply mode; WebSocket telemetry (replaces polling); `FailureClassifier` adds timeout category | | 2026.2 | 2026-02-09 | `AiRetentionPicker` length-aware curves; `ProxyAutoRefill` beta; drift threshold lowered to 2.5s | | 2026.1 | 2026-01-14 | 2026 baseline: geo-consistent fingerprint assembly, `ResumeEngine` hardened, encrypted vault migration | | 2025.4 | 2025-11-02 | `HeadlessRunner` CLI flags expanded; `ExportModule` CSV format | | 2025.3 | 2025-09-20 | `WarmUpWalker` added; `SessionPoolRecycler` stability fixes | | 2025.2 | 2025-07-11 | Proxy rotation strategies (sticky / round-robin / per-job) | | 2025.1 | 2025-05-04 | Initial public build — spawner, playback controller, SQLite job store | --- ## ❔ FAQ **1. Will this get my YouTube account banned?** The bot doesn't log into accounts — sessions are anonymous and never authenticate. There's no account to ban. The risk is to the *target video's* view count (views may be filtered), not to any personal account. **2. Why do my views show up then disappear after two days?** That's YouTube's delayed view validation. The most common causes are uniform retention (every session watching the same percentage) and proxy reuse across sessions. Switch to `AiRetentionPicker`, raise `watch_pct` variance, and check your proxy pool for shared endpoints. **3. Do I need residential proxies?** For a target video you actually care about, yes. Datacenter proxies work for testing the pipeline but get filtered at a much higher rate. Mobile proxies are the most reliable and the most expensive. **4. How many concurrent sessions should I run?** Default is 3. Below 3 is safer but slower; above 6 starts burning proxies faster than the health scorer can replace them. The `ThrottleGuard` exists to stop you from setting this too high by accident. **5. Does the AI stuff send my data anywhere?** No. The models are small, local, and compiled into the `.exe`. `AiRetentionPicker` and `AiProxyAdvisor` run entirely on-device. The only outbound traffic is the YouTube requests themselves. **6. Can I run this on a server without a display?** `HeadlessRunner` handles that — it's a CLI flag on the same `.exe`. No GUI is spawned. You'll want to run it via Task Scheduler or a service wrapper on Windows Server. **7. What happens if the job crashes halfway?** `JobStore` writes state after every completed session, and `ResumeEngine` picks up from the last one. You lose at most one session's worth of progress. **8. Why does the .exe trigger SmartScreen?** The build is unsigned. Signing certificates for this kind of tool are impractical to maintain. "More info → Run anyway" is the standard path; the binary is self-contained and does not modify system files. **9. Can I target a playlist or a channel instead of one video?** `PlaylistWalker` handles playlists and related-video targets. Channel-wide targeting is not supported in this build — jobs are scoped to a single video or playlist. **10. Where are my logs and job data stored?** Next to the `.exe`: `jobs.db` for job state, `logs/` for per-session logs, `sessions/` for browser profile caches. Nothing is written outside that folder, and the credential vault is AES-encrypted at rest. --- ## 💬 Community & Support - **Bug reports** — open an issue with the `DiagnosticsBundle` zip attached (wait 5s after job end, see Known Issues). - **Proxy provider discussion** — there's a pinned thread in Discussions for comparing residential/mobile providers by failure rate; keep it factual. - **Feature requests** — tag with `enhancement`; the module catalog above is the current scope, so requests that extend an existing module get prioritized over new subsystems. - **Build updates** — `UpdateChecker` polls the landing page; manual checks are in the About tab.

--- The 2026 build is the first where the AI subsystems actually change outcomes rather than just adding a checkbox — `AiRetentionPicker` in particular moves the needle on filtered views more than any proxy upgrade. If you're coming from an older build, the encrypted vault migration runs automatically on first launch, but back up `jobs.db` first. The module catalog above is the honest scope: 41 working modules, 2 in beta, and everything else is a wishlist item, not a shipped feature.

items.readme:
--- ## 🧭 Table of Contents - [Overview](#-overview) - [What Is Roblox Accounts Manager?](#-what-is-roblox-accounts-manager) - [The Problem](#-the-problem) - [The Solution](#-the-solution) - [Changelog / Release History](#-changelog--release-history) - [All Modules Status](#-all-modules-status) - [Account Core Modules](#-account-core-modules) - [Session & Cookie Modules](#-session--cookie-modules) - [Security & Privacy Modules](#-security--privacy-modules) - [Automation Modules](#-automation-modules) - [Compatibility / Platform Support](#-compatibility--platform-support) - [Detection / Bypass Status](#-detection--bypass-status) - [Performance Benchmarks](#-performance-benchmarks) - [Quick Start](#-quick-start) - [System Requirements](#-system-requirements) - [Installation](#-installation) - [Known Issues](#-known-issues) - [FAQ](#-faq) - [Community & Support](#-community--support) --- ## 🎮 Overview | Category | Details | |---|---| | **Project** | Roblox Accounts Manager — multi-account toolkit | | **Current build** | 2026 portable release (v2.0 rewrite) | | **Distribution** | Standalone `.exe` — no installer, no runtime | | **Platform** | Windows 10 / 11 (x64) | | **License** | MIT — open community project | | **Origin** | Forked from an abandoned 2023 codebase, fully rewritten | Roblox Accounts Manager started life as a half-finished script that broke every time Roblox rotated its web session cookies. The original repo went dark in 2023 with 40 open issues and zero merges. This 2026 build is a ground-up rewrite: the account store is now encrypted at rest, session rotation is handled natively instead of through a stale Python wrapper, and the whole thing ships as a single portable `.exe` with no installer and no runtime dependency. If you juggle alts, run a trading group, manage a clan roster, or just hate retyping the same password every time Roblox invalidates a cookie — this is the utility that was missing.
--- ## 📚 What Is Roblox Accounts Manager? | Term | Explanation | |---|---| | **Account Vault** | Encrypted local store holding every saved Roblox account profile | | **Session Cookie** | The `.ROBLOSECURITY` token that keeps a Roblox login alive | | **Profile** | One saved account: username, cookie, group memberships, notes, tags | | **Rotation** | Automatically refreshing a stale cookie without logging in again | | **Switcher** | The hotkey/tray mechanism that hot-swaps the active account | | **Alt Farm** | A batch of secondary accounts used for group or trading activity | | **Fingerprint Isolation** | Keeping per-account browser/device signals separated | Core benefits: - **One click, any account** — swap between saved profiles in under a second - **No re-login churn** — rotation keeps cookies alive so you stop hitting the login wall - **Grouped organization** — tag accounts as main / alt / trade / clan and filter instantly - **Portable by design** — the `.exe` runs from a USB stick, vault travels with it - **Batch import** — paste a list of cookie strings and the vault ingests them all - **No install footprint** — extract, run, done; nothing touches the registry --- ## 🩹 The Problem Anyone who actually runs multiple Roblox accounts knows the exact pain: - Roblox invalidates `.ROBLOSECURITY` cookies constantly, and every invalidation means a fresh login — usually right when you're mid-trade or mid-raid. - Browser profiles leak between accounts, so one alt logs out the main and you're stuck re-authenticating everything. - Password managers store credentials but *not* the live session, so they don't actually keep you logged in. - Group management requires hopping between 5–20 accounts to accept join requests or check payouts. - Spreadsheet-based alt tracking rots fast — passwords drift, notes get lost, and nobody remembers which alt owns which group. - Multi-boxing tools are built for one game and break on the next Roblox web update. - Existing "account switchers" are either malware bait or abandoned shells that stopped working in 2023. --- ## ✅ The Solution | Problem | Solution | |---|---| | Constant cookie invalidation | **Auto-Rotate** — background session refresh keeps profiles alive | | Browser profile leakage | **Isolated Switcher** — each profile launches in its own sandboxed context | | Password managers ignore sessions | **Session Vault** — stores live cookies, not just passwords | | Group admin hopping | **Batch Group Ops** — accept/leave/check across many accounts at once | | Spreadsheet alt rot | **Tagged Profile Store** — searchable vault with notes and group links | | Breakage on Roblox updates | **Hot-Patch Layer** — selector updates pushed independently of the `.exe` | | Malware-bait alternatives | **Open source** — auditable, signed releases, no obfuscated binaries | --- ## 📜 Changelog / Release History | Version | Date | Changes | |---|---|---| | **v2.0.4** | 2026-02 | Hot-patch layer stabilized; Everything else is built on top of a vault that never writes plaintext cookies to disk. - **Profile Vault** — AES-256-GCM encrypted store, key derived per-user - **Tag Manager** — main / alt / trade / clan / retired, plus custom tags - **Notes Attacher** — freeform notes so you stop guessing which alt owns what - **Recycle Bin** — 30-day restore window for accidental deletes - **Audit Log** — local-only record of logins, switches, and group actions ## 🍪 Session & Cookie Modules The original project died because Roblox kept changing how sessions expire. This build treats rotation as a first-class subsystem instead of a hacky side feature. - **Cookie Rotator** — background refresh on a configurable interval - **Session Monitor** — warns when a profile is within 24h of expiry - **2FA Helper** — prompts for a manual code when rotation needs it - **Clipboard Guard** — auto-clears copied cookie strings after 30s - **Auto-Login Launcher** — opens Roblox logged into the selected profile - **Hotkey Switcher** — global hotkey to swap active profiles - **Tray Switcher** — right-click from the system tray to change account ## 🔒 Security & Privacy Modules Nothing leaves the machine unless you explicitly export it. No wizard, no registry writes, no admin prompt. 2. **First launch** — you'll be prompted to create a vault password. It encrypts every saved cookie; there is no recovery if you lose it. 3. **Import accounts** — paste one cookie at a time, or paste a list into the Batch Importer. Tags and notes can be applied after import. 4. **Configure rotation** — the default interval is 6 hours; session monitor warns you when a profile is close to expiry.
